links.site_alt: amandaforalabama.com (named by the Daily Mountain Eagle)

oneliner.t: North Alabama nurse (campaign based in Cullman) who won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary over Shane Weaver in her first run for office, against Rep. Robert Aderholt.

born.t: 1990 — Missouri per the Daily Mountain Eagle; Ballotpedia lists her birthplace as Alabama (conflict unresolved)

hometown.t: North Alabama (Huntsville area; Bob Jones High School in Madison)

profile.residence: Cullman, AL area (campaign base; some sources say Huntsville)

upbringing.t: By her own account, Pusczek was born in 1990 to two alcoholic parents who divorced early, and moved to Alabama with her mother in 1996, where they lived through hard conditions. Her first taxable job, she says, was as a dishwasher at a Girl Scout camp at 13. She graduated from Bob Jones High School, earned an associate degree at Calhoun Community College (2014) and a bachelor's from Western Governors University (2022), and became a nurse working in hospitals, prisons and schools. She married her husband, Trever, in 2022 and says Alabama's reproductive-health restrictions and costs made starting a family difficult. These details are her own account as reported, not independently corroborated.

platform.t: Health-care workers should help shape laws; warns of rural hospital closures in the district; supports access to reproductive care including IVF.
Raise taxes on earners over $1 million and close loopholes, especially on capital gains.
Supports term limits for all elected and appointed officials.
Human rights, health care and science, and affordability; says Democrats did not seriously address Project 2025 in 2024.

promises.t: Raise taxes on income over $1 million and close capital-gains loopholes.
Support term limits for elected and appointed officials.

record.t: Employers not named; Alabama Board of Nursing license lookup not run.

Hospital licensure data not checked in this pass. Oct 8 update: Wikipedia's list of Alabama hospitals shows one Lamar County hospital, Lamar Regional Hospital in Vernon, listed as closed in 1996, and no open hospital in the county. The county article mentions no hospital. This points toward the claim being accurate, but it rests on a secondary list and an absence of entries. The Alabama Department of Public Health licensure directory was not reachable, so the verdict stays unverifiable.

claims.claim: A Republican state legislator said as many as 52 Alabama hospitals are at risk of closing.

record.t: The legislator and the source of the figure were not identified.

claims.claim: Nine more hospitals in the district could close within two years, leaving 10 of 13 counties without one.

record.t: A forecast, not a checkable fact.

claims.claim: The 4th District has 13 counties (the premise of her warning that 10 of 13 could lose hospitals).

said.where: speech to Walker County Democrats, Jasper (Daily Mountain Eagle)

record.t: The 119th-Congress district (unchanged for 2026) has 11 whole counties (Blount, Colbert, Cullman, DeKalb, Fayette, Franklin, Lamar, Marion, Marshall, Walker, Winston) plus parts of Lauderdale and Tuscaloosa, for 13 counties in all. The source page is inconsistent about Lauderdale, and the Census map it cites was not opened.

claims.claim: Her campaign site says Alabama's reproductive-care restrictions made starting a family hard for her and her husband, citing IVF costs, her high-risk status and clinic closures.

said.where: campaign website, as reported by the Daily Mountain Eagle

record.t: The checkable part is clinic closures. After the Alabama Supreme Court's Feb. 2024 LePage ruling, UAB and other Alabama IVF providers paused treatment. Two said they would resume right away once a protective law was signed on Mar. 6, 2024. The source reviewed documents pauses, not permanent closures. Her personal experience is not checkable.

checks.claims: Mechanical sample could not use the campaign site (citizensforapusczek.com / amandaforalabama.com unreachable). Used her Ballotpedia survey answers and her reported Jan. 2026 stump speech. No ads found. 5 checkable claims rated — all unverifiable with the records reachable — plus 1 forecast rated opinion. The campaign's public material is thin. Oct 8 pass: the campaign site was still unreachable (proxy refused; no web.archive.org access), and Ballotpedia lists no campaign URL. Re-read the full Daily Mountain Eagle story and her Ballotpedia survey (7 statements, all values or policy positions). Added 2 claims (1 true, 1 partly). Total: 8 claims, 2 rated true/partly, 5 unverifiable, 1 opinion. Still short of 5 checkable verdicts. The rest of her published material is personal history or policy positions, and the '52 hospitals at risk' figure cites an unnamed legislator.
checks.democracy: Reviewed her Ballotpedia survey and the Daily Mountain Eagle speech story. She said she found few candidates to vote for on her 2024 ballot and that Democrats didn't take Project 2025 seriously. Neither remark disputes or affirms the 2020 or 2024 results. Her campaign site was unreachable, and new news searches could not be run.

research_notes: MONEY: principal committee Citizens for Amanda Pusczek (C00902247), coverage 2025-10-01 to 2026-06-30. All contributions from individuals; 'other' = $70.67 offsets + $58.08 other receipts. The committee reports $12,000 in debts owed (creditor not identified) against $395.79 cash. Her FEC ID carries an AL05 prefix because she first filed in District 5 before switching to District 4 (statement of candidacy filed 2025-08-06). Track AIPAC does not list her. PROFILE: the Daily Mountain Eagle spelled her name 'Pasczek' in places. Photo not retrieved. WEB LIMITS (Oct 8, 2026 pass): the shared web-search budget was used up, and outbound connections to campaign sites, web.archive.org, census.gov, bls.gov, congress.gov and the House Clerk's disclosure search were blocked or refused. CLAIMS: fewer than 5 rated verdicts. The campaign site, the core of the mechanical sample, was never reached, so this is not a confirmed 'publishes fewer than 5' finding. checklist.claims stays 'news'. Discrepancy: she said in her speech that she was born in Missouri, while Ballotpedia lists her birthplace as Alabama. Ballotpedia names Bob Jones High School (Madison). DISCLOSURES: candidate financial disclosure not located; stays 'no'. DEMOCRACY: set to 'news'; no results statement found in coverage reviewed.
